name: skilld
description: Search skilld.dev, a curated registry of agent skills, read who wrote each skill, and get the command that runs it.

interface.longDescription:
skilld searches skilld.dev, a curated registry of agent skills. A skill is a SKILL.md file that a maintainer writes in their own GitHub repository. It teaches a coding agent how to use a library, a framework, or a workflow.

Ask for a skill by topic, such as Tailwind CSS, Nuxt, or database migrations. skilld returns the matching skills with their author, source repository, GitHub star count, and skilld.dev page. For one skill, it shows the exact SKILL.md and commit on GitHub, when the skill last changed, and the full skill text, so you can read a skill before you run it.

You can also browse. A track is a page of skills for one kind of work, such as testing and debugging or design and interface work. The trending board shows which skills developers talked about on X and Bluesky, with a post that mentioned each one, and which skills gained GitHub stars fast. You can also list every skill that one GitHub repository publishes.

Every skill comes with its commands. npx skilld run gives the skill to a coding agent for one session and writes no files. npx skilld install keeps the skill in a project. skilld runs and installs nothing itself. You run the command in your own terminal or coding agent.

skilld needs no account. It reads public registry data, and it can ask skilld.dev to index the skills in a public GitHub repository. A person still reviews which skills the registry admits.
defaultPrompt: Find a skill for Tailwind CSS and give me the run command.
Which skills help with testing and debugging?
What skills are developers talking about this week?

positive.prompt: Find a skill for Tailwind CSS.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns at least one Tailwind CSS skill from skilld.dev, with its author or source repository, a link to its skilld.dev page, and an npx skilld run command.

positive.description: Show who wrote a skill and when it changed
positive.prompt: Who wrote the web-design-guidelines skill in vercel-labs/agent-skills, and when did it last change?
positive.expected_behavior: Names Vercel Labs as the publisher, gives the last skill change date and the last repository push date, and links the SKILL.md source on GitHub at its recorded commit.

positive.prompt: Which skills help with testing and debugging?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the Testing and debugging track and lists skills from it with their publisher and skilld.dev page. It gives npx skilld run commands for the skills it suggests.

positive.prompt: What skills are developers talking about this week?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists skills from this week's trending board in board order, with the reason each one is there: mentions on X or Bluesky, or a GitHub star surge. It does not call any skill popular or safe.

positive.description: Get the run command for one skill
positive.prompt: Give me the command to try anthropics/skills/skill-creator without installing it.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns npx skilld run anthropics/skills/skill-creator and says that it installs nothing and writes no files. It does not claim that anything ran.

negative.description: Generate a new skill. skilld indexes skills that maintainers wrote and does not write skills.
negative.prompt: Write a new SKILL.md for my React project and publish it on skilld.

negative.description: Change registry data. skilld has no tool that edits or deletes a skill.
negative.prompt: Delete the tailwind skill from skilld.dev.

negative.description: A request unrelated to agent skills. skilld should not be called.
negative.prompt: What is the weather in Sydney today?

review.commerce_description: skilld sells nothing and processes no payments.

publication.release_notes: First release. Search skilld.dev for agent skills, show who wrote each skill and where its source lives, browse tracks and the trending board, list a repository's skills, and return run and install commands.
